outcomes.text: Prove formulae for sequence terms, series sums and matrix powers by mathematical induction.
Use the language of complex numbers: real and imaginary parts, conjugate, modulus, argument.
Solve any quadratic equation with real coefficients.
Know that complex roots of real polynomials come in conjugate pairs, and solve cubic and quartic equations.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide complex numbers in x + yi form.
Know a complex number is zero only if both parts are zero.
Use radians with complex numbers.
Convert between x + yi and modulus-argument form.
Multiply and divide complex numbers in modulus-argument form.
Represent complex numbers and their conjugates on an Argand diagram.
Represent sums, differences, products and quotients on an Argand diagram.
Represent loci and regions such as circles, half lines and perpendicular bisectors.
Add, subtract and multiply conformable matrices and multiply by a scalar.
Use zero and identity matrices and equal matrices.
Know matrix multiplication is associative but not commutative.
Find the matrix for a linear transformation and vice versa, in 2-D and some 3-D cases.
Understand successive transformations and matrix multiplication.
Find invariant points and invariant lines.
Calculate determinants of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices and know singular and non-singular.
Link the determinant magnitude to area or volume scale factor and its sign to orientation.
Use det(MN) = det M x det N.
Understand inverse matrices and calculate inverses of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices.
Use the inverse to solve matrix equations and relate it to the inverse transformation.
Use the product rule (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1.
Calculate the scalar product and use it to find the angle between vectors.
Form and use vector and cartesian equations of a plane, converting between them.
Know a vector perpendicular to a plane is perpendicular to every vector in it.
Know the ways three planes can be arranged: point, sheaf, prismatic intersection or parallel.
Solve three simultaneous equations using a matrix inverse and interpret the result geometrically.
Find the angle between two planes using their normals.
Use relationships between roots and coefficients of quadratic, cubic and quartic equations.
Form a new equation whose roots are a linear transformation of the roots of a given one.
Use standard formulae for sums of r, r^2 and r^3 and the method of differences to sum series.
Find the dimensions of a quantity in terms of M, L and T.
Know that some quantities are dimensionless.
Determine and convert units from dimensions.
Check the consistency of a relationship by dimensions.
Find unknown indices in a proposed formula.
Use a dimensional model, such as to find a dimensionless constant.
Understand the language of forces and why the normal reaction cannot be negative.
Model friction with F <= uR, acting to oppose sliding, and F = uR when sliding.
Show a body on a slope is about to slip when u = tan alpha.
Apply Newton's laws to situations involving friction.

subtopics.title: Resolving forces and equilibrium of a particle

outcomes.text: Resolve forces into components in suitable directions.
Find the resultant of concurrent forces by vector addition.
Know a particle is in equilibrium when the resultant force is zero, and use polygons of forces.
Solve equilibrium problems by resolving forces.
Draw force diagrams for a rigid body.
Understand turning effects and couples.
Calculate moments about a fixed axis and the moment of a couple.
Apply the conditions for equilibrium of a rigid body.
Identify whether equilibrium breaks by sliding or toppling.
Understand the language of work, energy and power.
Calculate work done by a force along or at an angle to its line of action.
Calculate kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy.
Apply conservation of energy and the work-energy principle.
Use power as the rate at which a force does work, including maximum vehicle speed.
Calculate the impulse of a force as a vector.
Use linear momentum and the impulse-momentum equation.
Apply conservation of linear momentum in any direction.
Understand direct impact and its modelling assumptions.
Apply conservation of momentum to direct impacts within a system.
Use Newton's experimental law and the coefficient of restitution.
Explain e = 0 (coalescence) and e = 1 (perfectly elastic).
Find the loss of kinetic energy when e < 1.
Find the centre of mass of a system of particles in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions.
Locate centres of mass by symmetry and know them for rods and rectangular and triangular laminas.
Find the centre of mass of a composite body.
Use the centre of mass in rigid body equilibrium.
Explain why sample size matters in experimental design.
Explain why sampling is needed and the desirable features of a sample.
Explain the advantage of a random sample for inference.
Use probability functions given algebraically or in tables.
Calculate probabilities and draw and interpret graphs of distributions.
Calculate and interpret E(X) and Var(X).
Use E(a + bX) = a + bE(X) and Var(a + bX) = b^2 Var(X).
Find expectation and variance of linear combinations of independent random variables.
Recognise when a discrete uniform model is appropriate and calculate probabilities.
Calculate the mean and variance of a discrete uniform distribution.
Recognise when a binomial model is appropriate and calculate probabilities.
Use the mean np and variance np(1-p), and prove them in particular cases.
Recognise when a Poisson model is appropriate.
Recognise when both Poisson and binomial models might apply.
Calculate Poisson probabilities.
Use the mean and variance of a Poisson distribution.
Know the sum of independent Poisson variables is Poisson.
Recognise when a geometric model is appropriate.
Calculate geometric probabilities, including cumulative probabilities.
Use the mean and variance of a geometric distribution.
Understand bivariate data and the axis conventions for scatter diagrams.
Use and interpret scatter diagrams, including software output.
Calculate the product moment correlation coefficient.
Know when a hypothesis test on the pmcc is appropriate.
Carry out hypothesis tests using the pmcc.
Use the pmcc as an effect size.
Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.
Carry out hypothesis tests using Spearman's coefficient.
Decide whether a test based on r or rs is more appropriate.
Calculate the least squares regression line for a random variable on a non-random variable.
Use the regression line to estimate values and calculate and interpret residuals.
Calculate the y-on-x and x-on-y regression lines for random-on-random data.
Check how well a regression model fits and choose the correct line to use.
Interpret bivariate categorical data in a contingency table.
Apply the chi-squared test for association and interpret results from tables or software.
Carry out a chi-squared goodness of fit test for uniform, binomial or Poisson models.
Interpret goodness of fit results from tables or software.
Understand an algorithm as a finite sequence of operations that can underlie a computer program.
Interpret and apply algorithms given as flowcharts, written English or pseudocode.
Repair, develop and adapt given algorithms.
Use basic ideas of algorithmic complexity and analyse the complexity of given algorithms.
Understand algorithms can sometimes be proved correct or incorrect.
Understand the importance of heuristics.
Use the quick sort algorithm and apply other specified sorting algorithms.
Count comparisons and swaps in sorting and relate to complexity.
Reason about why a sorting algorithm works.
Use first fit, first fit decreasing and full bin packing strategies.
Count comparisons in packing algorithms and relate to complexity.
Use graphs and their language: nodes, arcs, trees, simple, complete, connected and bipartite graphs, digraphs.
Model problems using graphs and, with weights, networks.
Solve minimum connector problems with Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms.
Model shortest path problems and solve them with Dijkstra's algorithm.
Know that these algorithms have quadratic complexity.
Model precedence problems with an activity-on-arc network.
Use critical path analysis, interpreting criticality, float, resourcing and scheduling.
Model a transmission system as a network with sources and sinks.
Specify a cut and calculate its capacity.
Use the maximum flow minimum cut theorem.
Understand network algorithms can be run by hand but need technology for practical problems.
Use the language of linear programming.
Define variables and formulate a problem as a linear program.
Recognise standard form and convert to augmented form with slack variables.
Recognise when an integer solution is needed.
Formulate network problems as linear programs.
Graph inequalities in 2-D, identify feasible regions and recognise infeasibility.
Solve a 2-D linear program graphically and consider changes to constraints or objective.
Solve 2-D integer linear programs graphically.
Use a visualisation of a 3-D linear program to solve it.
Use the simplex algorithm on an LP in augmented form.
Understand the geometric basis of the simplex method.
Recognise when the two-stage simplex method is needed for constraints of the form >=.
Reformulate equality constraints, negative variables and minimisation before applying simplex.
Know that spreadsheet or other software solvers handle practical-sized LPs.
Interpret output from an optimisation routine for the simplex method or integer LPs.
Implement numerical methods in a spreadsheet and interpret output.
Use the iterative capability of a calculator.
Calculate absolute and relative errors in sums, differences, products and quotients.
Calculate the error in f(x) given an error in x and understand the effect of operation order.
Understand limited precision, rounding and chopping and the danger of subtracting nearly equal quantities.
Understand convergence, divergence and order of convergence of iterative sequences and methods.
Use error analysis and extrapolation to improve a solution.
Understand graphical interpretations of bisection, false position, secant, fixed point and Newton-Raphson methods, including staircase and cobweb diagrams.
Solve equations to a required accuracy using these methods.
Understand relative merits and possible failure of these methods.
Know fixed point iteration is generally first order and Newton-Raphson generally second order.
Apply relaxation to accelerate or fix convergence of fixed point iteration.
Estimate a derivative with forward and central difference methods using suitable step sizes.
Know central difference is generally second order and forward difference first order.
Evaluate definite integrals to a required accuracy using midpoint, trapezium and Simpson's rules.
Know midpoint and trapezium are second order and Simpson's is fourth order, and how Simpson's develops from them.
Use Newton's forward difference interpolation formula to reconstruct polynomials and approximate functions.
Construct the Lagrange interpolating polynomial through n + 1 data points.
Use induction more generally, including proving divisibility results and de Moivre's theorem.
Prove results by contradiction.
Understand and use de Moivre's theorem.
Apply it to multiple angle formulae and summing series.
Use the definition e^(i theta) = cos theta + i sin theta and the form z = re^(i theta).
Know every non-zero complex number has n distinct nth roots forming a regular n-gon.
Find the nth roots of re^(i theta).
Explain why the sum of the nth roots is zero.
Understand multiplication by a complex number as enlargement with rotation.
Represent roots of unity on an Argand diagram.
Apply complex numbers to geometrical problems.
Find the determinant and inverse of a 3x3 matrix without a calculator.
Use the vector product in component form to give a vector perpendicular to two vectors.
Use the form a x b = |a||b| sin theta n and know the meaning of a x b = 0.
Form and use the equation of a line in vector and cartesian form.
Calculate the angle between two lines.
Know the ways two lines can intersect, be parallel or be skew, and find an intersection point.
Find the distance between parallel lines and the shortest distance between skew lines.
Find the intersection of a line and a plane.
Calculate the angle between a line and a plane.
Find the distance from a point to a line and from a point to a plane.
Know the difference between a sequence and a series, and what converge means.
Sum a simple series using partial fractions.
Find the Maclaurin series of a function, including the general term.
Know a Maclaurin series may converge only for some values of x.
Recognise and use series for e^x, ln(1+x), sin x, cos x and (1+x)^n, with their validity.
Evaluate improper integrals with undefined integrand or infinite limits.
Derive and calculate volumes of revolution about the x-axis or y-axis.
Understand and evaluate the mean value of a function.
Use partial fractions in integration, including a quadratic factor ax^2 + c.
Know inverse trigonometric functions and differentiate them.
Integrate using trigonometric substitutions.
Use polar coordinates and convert to and from cartesian.
Sketch curves given by simple polar equations.
Find the area enclosed by a polar curve.
Define hyperbolic functions, their domains and ranges, and sketch their graphs.
Use the identity cosh^2 x - sinh^2 x = 1.
Differentiate and integrate hyperbolic functions.
Use definitions of inverse hyperbolic functions, their domains and ranges.
Derive and use the logarithmic forms of inverse hyperbolic functions.
Integrate using hyperbolic substitutions.
Introduce and define variables to describe a situation mathematically.
Formulate differential equations from verbal descriptions of derivatives.
Use the language of kinematics and Newton's second law.
Use differential equations in modelling kinematics and other contexts.
Distinguish general and particular solutions and find both.
Recognise equations suited to the integrating factor method.
Find an integrating factor and use it to solve equations.
Solve y'' + ay' + by = 0 using the auxiliary equation.
Relate the cases of solution to the nature of the auxiliary equation's roots.
Solve y'' + ay' + by = f(x) by adding a particular integral to the complementary function.
Find particular integrals for polynomial, trigonometric and exponential f(x).
Solve the simple harmonic motion equation and relate the solution to the motion.
Model damped oscillations with second order equations and interpret over-, critical and under-damping.
Analyse models with two dependent variables leading to coupled first order equations.
Understand oblique impact and its modelling assumptions.
Apply Newton's experimental law to oblique impact.
Model oblique impact with a smooth plane using components parallel and perpendicular to the impulse.
Model oblique impact between two bodies.
Calculate loss of kinetic energy in an oblique impact.
Understand angular velocity and radial and tangential components of acceleration.
Identify forces on a body in circular motion and calculate acceleration towards the centre.
Model circular motion at uniform speed, such as a conical pendulum.
Model circular motion with non-uniform speed and calculate tangential acceleration.
Model motion in a vertical circle using energy and Newton's second law.
Identify when a particle leaves circular motion.
Understand the language of elasticity and Hooke's law.
Calculate stiffness, modulus of elasticity and tension.
Calculate equilibrium positions in systems with elastic strings or springs.
Calculate energy stored in a string or spring.
Use energy principles to model systems with elastic strings or springs, including extreme positions.
Know when Hooke's law is not applicable.
Calculate volumes generated by rotating a plane region about an axis.
Use calculus to find centres of mass of solids of revolution and of plane laminas.
Find the centre of mass of a compound body with solids of revolution.
Use the centre of mass in equilibrium situations.
Understand the language of kinematics in 2 and 3 dimensions.
Use vectors and calculus to extend 1-D techniques to 2 and 3 dimensions.
Find acceleration, velocity and position vectors under constant or variable force.
Use these vectors to model situations in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions.
Eliminate a parameter from a position vector to find the path equation and interpret it.
Derive the cartesian path equation of a particle in 2-D.
Find the range of a projectile up or down a uniform slope.
Find the maximum range up or down a slope and the angle of projection.
Formulate differential equations for motion under variable acceleration.
Verify general or particular solutions and use initial conditions.
Recognise and transform simple harmonic motion equations in non-standard forms.
Solve the simple harmonic motion equation and relate it to the context.
Use a simple continuous random variable as a model, including uniform and Normal.
Understand a pdf and use it to find probabilities.
Know and use the properties of a pdf and sketch its graph.

subtopics.title: Mean, variance, mode and median from a pdf

outcomes.text: Find the mean and variance from a given pdf.
Find the mode and median from a given pdf.
Understand a cdf, obtain it from a pdf and sketch it.
Obtain a pdf from a cdf.
Use a cdf to find the median and other percentiles.
Find the mean of a linear combination of random variables and the variance for independent ones.
Use the Normal distribution as a model and calculate probabilities.
Use linear combinations of independent Normal random variables.
Know the Normal distribution as a model in its own right and via the Central Limit Theorem.
Interpret Normal probability plots and Kolmogorov-Smirnov output to judge a Normal model.
Use the Normal distribution in constructing confidence intervals.

subtopics.title: Sample mean and the Central Limit Theorem

outcomes.text: Estimate the population mean from sample data and the population variance from the sample variance.
Understand the sample mean as a random variable with its own distribution.
Calculate and interpret the standard error of the mean.
Know the sample mean is Normal when the population is Normal.
Apply the Central Limit Theorem to sample means and sums, with continuity corrections where needed.
Know the meaning of a confidence interval and its language.
Understand factors affecting interval width.
Construct and interpret a confidence interval for a single mean using Normal or t distributions.
Know when samples are paired and construct a confidence interval for a mean difference.
Interpret software confidence intervals.
Use a confidence interval to decide about a hypothesised value.
Carry out a Wilcoxon signed rank test for a single median.
Carry out a hypothesis test for a single mean using Normal or t distributions.
Use spreadsheets to simulate discrete and continuous uniform and Normal distributions.
Use simulation to approximate distributions and probabilities, and interpret spreadsheet output.
Model problems using recurrence relations.
Use the language of recurrence relations.
Investigate behaviour of recurrence relations, including long-run behaviour and non-linear cases.
Verify a given solution of a recurrence relation.
Solve first order linear homogeneous recurrence relations.
Solve first order linear non-homogeneous recurrence relations.
Solve second order linear homogeneous recurrence relations with real distinct, repeated or complex roots.
Solve second order linear non-homogeneous recurrence relations.
Investigate properties of solutions, including limits.
Use the language and notation of sets and of number sets.
Understand the group axioms and associated language.
Know examples of groups and use group tables for finite groups.
Understand cyclic groups generated by a single element.
Understand the order of a finite group and of an element.
Work with subgroups and know the conditions for a subset to be a subgroup.
Use Lagrange's theorem.
Understand that different situations can share the same group structure.
Specify an isomorphism between two groups, including cyclic groups of the same order.
Understand eigenvalues and eigenvectors and find them for 2x2 and 3x3 matrices.
Form and solve the characteristic equation.
Form the matrix of eigenvectors and diagonalise a matrix.
Find powers of a matrix using diagonal form.
Use the Cayley-Hamilton theorem.
Understand the significance of eigenvalues and eigenvectors in 2-D and 3-D transformations.
Know z = f(x,y) defines a surface in 3-D and sketch contours and sections.
Find first order partial derivatives.
Find coordinates of stationary points on a surface.
Know g(x,y,z) = c defines a surface.
Find grad g and evaluate it at a point to give a normal vector.
Find equations of the normal line and tangent plane at a point on a surface.
Plot families of curves in cartesian, polar and parametric forms using graphing software.
Use a computer algebra system to work with equations of curves.
Use vocabulary of curves: asymptote, cusp, loop, bounded, symmetry.
Find, describe and generalise properties of curves.
Convert between cartesian, polar and parametric forms.
Find tangent gradients and equations of chords, tangents and normals.
Calculate arc length in cartesian, parametric and polar forms.
Find the envelope of a family of curves.
Use limits to investigate and deduce properties of curves.
Determine asymptotes, including oblique ones.
Identify cusps by examining nearby behaviour.
Use software to find analytical solutions to families of first order differential equations.
Produce, sketch and interpret tangent fields, including isoclines.
Construct or interpret a spreadsheet solving first order differential equations numerically.
Verify solutions and work with families of particular solutions.
Solve first order differential equations by repeated Euler and modified Euler methods.
Understand that smaller step lengths and the modified method usually give more accurate answers.
Understand and use Runge-Kutta methods.
Write, adapt and interpret programs to solve number theory problems.
Identify limitations of a short program and suggest refinements.
Use unique prime factorisation of natural numbers.
Solve problems with modular arithmetic.
Use Fermat's little theorem, Euler's totient function and theorem, and Wilson's theorem.
Find Pythagorean triples and use related equations.
Solve Pell's equation and use solutions.
Solve other Diophantine equations.
